title: Gastric Glomus Tumor Mimicking a Neuroendocrine Tumor: A Diagnostic Pitfall Associated with Synaptophysin Expression
content: Background and Clinical Significance: Gastric glomus tumors (GGTs) are uncommon mesenchymal neoplasms that may mimic gastric neuroendocrine tumors because of overlapping morphologic and immunohistochemical features. Case Presentation: We describe a 73-year-old man with a 1.5 cm well-circumscribed submucosal mass in the gastric antrum, resected after a nondiagnostic fine needle biopsy. Histologic examination showed uniform round cells arranged in nests around prominent vascular channels, with rare mitoses and no significant atypia or necrosis. Tumor cells showed moderate to strong synaptophysin expression and were positive for smooth muscle actin and calponin. Chromogranin A, INSM1, pancytokeratin, Cam5.2, CD117, and DOG1 were negative, and the Ki-67 proliferation index was less than 2%. These findings supported a diagnosis of gastric glomus tumor. Conclusions: This case highlights the importance of integrating morphology with a broader immunohistochemical panel, including more than one neuroendocrine marker and smooth muscle markers, rather than relying on synaptophysin alone.
